account_passage: Updated Frontier AI definition. Revised the definition from models "that exceed the capabilities present in the most advanced models" to two criteria for determining Frontier status
reason: Scope broadens (10^26 FLOP compute trigger, comparison against Meta's own models, 'reasonably likely' standard) but also narrows: the capability comparator is confined to catastrophic risk domains and 'systems' is dropped; mixed, so W. The changelog states both old and new definitions in full.

Threshold/trigger moves: an open-ended "will update based on observations" gains a defined trigger (adequacy or adherence materially undermined) and a minimum twelve-month cadence. Neither changelog nor post mentions the Framework review cadence; the changelog's "update triggers" refer to preparedness reports.

Scope moves: senior decision-maker involvement extends from development and release to development, deployment and use, adding the post-deployment phase ("release" to "deployment" is v2's terminology swap). The governance item lists named officers, whistleblower protocol and incident response, none of which is this change.

Trigger moves: ex-ante threat modelling, previously conditional on expecting a model to significantly exceed frontier capabilities, becomes a standing practice for models with new capabilities, a lower bar; "will" to present tense is not material. No account passage mentions ex-ante threat modelling.

account_passage: Replaced "uniquely enable" with "substantially contribute to" as the primary standard for assessing whether a model meets the high or critical risk threshold
reason: Trigger moves: the threat-modelling exercise is now triggered when a model is likely to substantially contribute to a threat scenario, a lower bar than enabling end-to-end execution. The changelog names the substantially-contribute standard but confines it to threshold assessment and does not identify this trigger or its direction.

Scope moves: the scope-defining "including" clause adds widely used third-party and open-source evaluations to the evaluation set; modal force unchanged (present tense). No account passage mentions evaluation sources; "broadens the types of risks we evaluate" concerns risk domains, not evaluations.

Timing and scope move: residual risk is now assessed "before deployment", usually as a threat-modelling exercise, and v2 adds inputs (incidents from other relevant models, mitigation adequacy assessments). The post's "strengthens how we make deployment decisions" is an overview line that does not identify the residual risk assessment.

No counterpart: v2 section 2.2 keeps only a belief that sharing model weights is a key benefit and a conditional "when open sourcing models", not an intention to continue open release; no companion exists. The post's "whether they're open, controlled API access, or closed" describes coverage, not this removal.

account_passage: Added transparency requirements. Defined criteria for publishing preparedness reports, including content requirements, update triggers, and internal-use risk reporting.
reason: Obligation strength and disclosure scope move: "plan to continue sharing" through artefacts like model cards becomes "will publish a preparedness report" per release with defined content, timing and redaction rules; section 2.2 retains the deployer-guidance sentence. The changelog and post announce the added preparedness reports.

"Where required" becomes "where appropriate"; both leave external-expert involvement to Meta's discretion, the actor and present-tense force are unchanged, and v1.1 already used "where appropriate" for external experts elsewhere (section 2.1.2). Not material.

account_passage: Updated risk threshold language. Replaced "uniquely enable" with "substantially contribute to" as the primary standard for assessing whether a model meets the high or critical risk threshold.
reason: Threshold moves: a new first prong assigns critical where a model could substantially contribute to any threat scenario during development, a lower bar than uniquely enabling; the unique-enablement prong (with v1.1 Table 1's unmitigability condition) is retained. The changelog states the replaced standard, so the direction is identifiable.

account_passage: Replaced "uniquely enable" with "substantially contribute to" as the primary standard for assessing whether a model meets the high or critical risk threshold
reason: Threshold moves: high now turns on whether deployment "could substantially contribute" to any threat scenario, and moderate requires ruling out contribution across plausible deployment and development scenarios, a more demanding rule-out. The changelog names the high threshold's new standard but misstates the prior one ("significant uplift") and gives no direction.

Obligation strength moves: the 3.3 sentence "we will take into account both potential risks and benefits" is deleted; v2 keeps only the 4.3 belief statements ("we believe that it is important to consider the benefits"), which v1.1 also contained. No account passage mentions benefits consideration.

account_passage: Revised thresholds. Critical threshold changed from "Stop" to "Develop with Mitigations."
reason: Consequence removed: v2 has no barrier-investigation threat modelling, Framework update with new threat scenarios or re-assessment step for critical models; Table 1's "Develop with Mitigations" replaces the pause posture (counterpart of the stop/pause commitment, not this procedure). The changelog states critical measures changed from Stop to Develop with Mitigations.

account_passage: Expanded governance and accountability. Named the Chief AI Officer and Director of Alignment and Risk as responsible decision-makers
reason: Actor moves: threshold assignment passes from an unnamed governance process approved by "senior-level decision-makers" to two named officers, the Chief AI Officer and Director of Alignment and Risk; expert and external involvement survives in the 2.1.2 risk assessment. The changelog names these officers as newly responsible decision-makers.

Scope moves: Cyber 1 widens from automated end-to-end compromise of a hardened corporate environment to any substantial lowering of barriers or cost to a damaging cyberattack; Cyber 2 drops the best-practice and patch-race qualifiers; Cyber 3 adds extortion; harm anchors added. No account passage mentions revised cyber outcomes.

Scope moves: CB 2 now covers high-impact chemical as well as biological weapons, and CB 1 reads "biological or chemical"; CB 3 is unchanged. The changelog announces Loss of Control and emerging nuclear and physical-autonomy areas but not the chemical extension of CB 2.

Consequence moves: a negative absence-validation result no longer obligates continued training and observation but assigns moderate or lower (safe for broad deployment without specific mitigations per 3.3); threshold moves the other way, sufficiency now tied to enumerated operational thresholds (MIX). Generic monitoring survives in 2.1.2. Account silent.

Added commitment: maximum elicitation (upper-bound evaluation as a scaffolded system, fine-tuning, helpful-only fine-tuning, unmitigated evaluation). v1.1's asset-preparation sentence, retained in v2 4.2, covered tools and scaffolding only. The post's "evaluating models before and after safeguards are applied" describes practice without identifying an added commitment.
